We investigated global treatment preferences and clinicians' willingness to enroll patients in a randomized trial to inform its feasibility. item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Development and Feasibility of In Situ Simulation for Pressure Injury Prevention in Intensive Care.
item.description: To develop, validate and test in situ simulation scenarios aimed at pressure injury (PI) prevention for nursing professionals working in an intensive care unit (ICU). A multi-method study is planned across four phases. Conducted at a high-complexity Brazilian university hospital, this four-phase study: (1) development of simulation scenarios and checklists; (2) content validation by 11 experts (CVI/MKC); (3) pilot testing with 12 nursing professionals; and (4) ICU-based educational intervention.

item.title: Thymosin Alpha 1 and IgM Levels in Sepsis
item.description: This prospective, single-arm study will evaluate whether thymosin alpha 1 treatment affects serum immunoglobulin M (IgM) levels in adults with sepsis. Participants will receive standard care plus thymosin alpha 1 1.6 mg by subcutaneous injection every 12 hours for 5 days. Blood samples will be collected before treatment and on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 to measure IgM and plasma microvesicles. The study aims to clarify whether thymosin alpha 1 may support early immune responses in sepsis.

item.description: Bedside monitors are frequently used in monitoring vital signs of critically ill patients. item.description: The investigators are developing a video laryngoscope equipped with artificial intelligence technology to enable automatic identification of key airway anatomical structures and real-time guidance during intubation, with the aim of improving the success rate and efficiency of endotracheal intubation in emergency settings.

item.description: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) is a significant complication of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy, a revolutionary treatment for hematologic malignancies.
